issue: Missing a derived tired-light transfer mechanism.
solution: Write a microscopic or effective interaction action/collision kernel and a complete transport equation for spectral intensity I(ν,n,t). Predict spectrum, flux, redshift, arrival duration, polarization and image width from the **same coefficients**. Freeze them before a blind comparison.

issue: Supernova light-curve durations are an exceptionally stringent benchmark.
solution: Require an ArcSecs mechanism to derive b, not add (1+z) manually. Include held-out light-curve samples and test scatter/residuals by band and redshift. Primary: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05050 .

issue: No single completed nonmetric gravity law.
solution: Choose one Lagrangian or interaction, derive equations of motion and conservation, calculate perihelion advance, PPN limits, solar bending, Shapiro delay, binary inspirals, lensing and clock results. Do not put the missing factor of two in manually.

issue: Massive photons do not automatically cause tired light or cold dark matter.
solution: Specify whether mass is an invariant physical mass, an effective in-medium mass, or a new dark species; publish the model-dependent mass constraint table and a conservation-compatible formation pathway. Source: https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/listings/rpp2025-list-photon.pdf .

issue: The dark-light-to-dark-matter conversion lacks an inventory.
solution: Write a Boltzmann/evolution equation and calculate Ω_dark and phase-space distribution, structure growth, strong/weak lensing, galaxy-halo requirements and unobserved diffuse heating; fail the hypothesis if one mechanism cannot close all ledgers.

issue: No established local faster-than-light anomaly.
solution: Present FTL as a clearly scoped candidate law, require a reproducible local light-signal comparison with synchronization controls, laboratory energy–momentum tests, and a precisely specified prediction outside established theory.

issue: Dark Matter Drive lacks a demonstrated substrate capture force and positive net thrust.
solution: Determine ρ, interaction cross-section, effective aperture, power, drag, exhaust momentum and thermal load independently. Illustrative upper encounter rate only (not a usable fuel rate): assume local halo density ρ=0.3 GeV/cm³ ≈5.35×10^-22 kg/m³, circular radius 2,000 km, v=0.1c, η=1; then ṁ≈0.20 kg/s. This is not a void-specific density, and η=1 has no experimental basis. The captured flow carries an incoming momentum rate of roughly 6×10^6 N under these extreme idealized assumptions; a thrust ledger must include that influence rather than call all ejecta momentum free thrust.

issue: The β→0 deep-void inertia collapse is not derived.
solution: Integrate an explicit cosmological density distribution and realistic kernel, show uncertainty and boundary effects, and preregister an inertia-variation test before any FTL performance claims.

issue: Foreground-contamination / high-z taxonomy omitted from the book.
solution: Add the full cases and observation-stage labels from the table above; keep the z=7.04 spectroscopically confirmed Abell 2744–QSO1 alongside the false candidates to show the criterion is methodological, not cherry-picking.

issue: Distances and 'little red dots' can be conflated with different samples.
solution: Use separately defined catalog classes and source-by-source labels including photometric/spectroscopic z, line ID, confidence, lensing corrections, proper motion, host-galaxy light, AGN contamination, and revision history.

issue: The claim 'some red objects were nearby planets' is too broad.
solution: Use 'nearby substellar brown dwarfs' and mention 'possible rogue planet' only as a historical proposed interpretation in the specific cited case.

issue: Multi-messenger photon-slowing needs the source-delay uncertainty.
solution: Treat source delay, environment, gravitational path, detector clocks, and propagation as separate probabilistic nuisance terms; use confirmed, preferably multiply imaged counterparts and explicit likelihood models. Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834 .

issue: CCC+TL is not automatically evidence for a static or completely nonmetric universe.
solution: Separate classical static tired light, expanding CCC+TL hybrid, and proposed ArcSecs nonmetric branch, with independent free parameters and fit statistics. Primary: https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/524/3/3385/7221343 .

issue: Varying dimensional constants require operational definitions.
solution: Specify the actually changing dimensionless quantities, independent laboratory/astronomical bounds, units, simultaneous changes in spectra and clock dynamics, and one falsifiable signature.

issue: Missing complete cosmological observable predictions.
solution: Build a documented forward model with full selection effects, publish training/holdout splits, fit criteria and parameter cost, and compare residuals on a common dataset. Include redshift-dependent angular diameter distance and luminosity distance as separate outputs.

issue: Misleading 'corrected reports' scope in the handoff.
solution: Relabel them 'executive advocacy summaries' immediately. Then create full, line-tracked revisions of the original 14 astrophysics reports, retaining useful equations, citations, numerical cases, and noting removed/fixed claims with a change log. Keep the unrelated governance report as a separate archive.

issue: Book lacks claim-level citations.
solution: Add numbered in-text endnotes for every observation, quantitative statistic, non-obvious historical assertion, and model-specific claim; make a primary-source bibliography with DOI, date, observing program, and evidential status.

issue: Test plans are not test results.
solution: Make a reproducibility repository: environment/requirements, source DOI, checksum, unit tests for parallax and energy bookkeeping, preregistration, model parameter files, datasets and figures, machine-readable pass/fail output. No simulation victory claim before these results exist.

issue: The philosophical target needs an exact definition.
solution: Keep the ArcSecs title as an advocacy headline, but place the precise claim in bold: *The success of metric geometry does not prove an independent material substance called spacetime; ArcSecs seeks a nonmetric mechanism with distinctive, testable predictions*. Separate ontology from empirical tests throughout.

issue: Inter-model contradiction risk.
solution: Version a model decision tree. Lock one core theory per numerical comparison: A = classical static TL; B = expanding CCC+TL; C = nonmetric relational TL; D = Proca+interaction; E = Machian gravity. Publish a compatibility and parameter matrix before combining models.

issue: Redshift-inference uncertainties need explicit probability distributions.
solution: For each object record P(z|photometry,templates), alternative low-z and brown-dwarf model fits, NIRSpec line IDs, temporal baselines, proper motion, covariance and final label; never replace a posterior distribution with one extreme best-fit number.

issue: Geometry-first distance methods are calibrated, but are not a general substitute for all high-z distances.
solution: Maintain a four-stage measurement ladder: direct parallax; calibrated distance; geometric standard sirens and other anchors; cosmology-dependent luminosity/angular-distance inference, each with uncertainty.

issue: Manuscript is book-formatted but still an extended research edition.
solution: Reduce repeated slogans, add 3–5 full case studies (Capotauro, GW170817, supernova timing, lensing, galaxy rotation), real figures with permissions, and a complete numerical model specification. Preserve the one-sided ArcSecs position.

issue: Website completeness and provenance remain limited.
solution: Export WordPress content, attachments and media inventory; record article permalink, revision date, author, citations and retrieved timestamp. Reconcile the export to the source digest.
